card.title: I Survived This First
card.instruction: Use your experience with hardship as emotional seniority, offering guidance and judging how well others are handling the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went through redundancy before you. First, tidy your desk slowly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Early stage. I recognise the optimism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another job. They want me there Monday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday? I started too soon after mine. Leave a mug here; you're not ready to make a clean break.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims redundancy seniority, A3 classifies excitement as an early stage, and A5 uses A's too-soon restart to prescribe an incomplete departure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's excitement prompts A3's stage diagnosis; B4's new job and Monday start cause A5's leave-a-mug advice.

relationship.evidence: B2 states a positive reaction and B4 supplies the concrete reason for it.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's quick next job as further evidence that B needs A's experienced caution.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes redundancy and desk clearing; B4 identifies the actual next employment date.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's mug left behind turns the psychological judgment into a specific workplace act.
